In this case, the term $9{x}^{8}$ outside the parentheses isn't quite the derivative of $9+2{x}^{9}.$ But the derivative is $18{x}^{8},$ so we're only out by a constant factor.
So we make the substitution

$$
u=9+2{x}^{9}.
$$

Its derivative is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =18{x}^{8}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=9{x}^{8}\,\text{d}x,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can now write our integral in terms of $u,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 9{x}^{8}(9+2{x}^{9})^{3}\,\text{d}x & =\int (9+2{x}^{9})^{3}\cdot 9{x}^{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {u}^{3}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int {u}^{3}\,\text{d}u\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve the integral in terms of $u$ and then write the final result in terms of $x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\int {u}^{3}\,\text{d}u & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{{u}^{4}}{4}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{u}^{4}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(9+2{x}^{9})^{4}+C \\  & =\frac{(9+2{x}^{9})^{4}}{8}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
